stops.note: a store; at Delphi, cities built small temple-like 'treasuries' for their offerings, such as the Athenian Treasury of about 490 BC
borrowed from Greek for a hoard; centuries later, in 1852, Peter Mark Roget chose it as the title of his word-finder
via Old French tresor; the Norman kings kept their treasure at Winchester, and the Exchequer's accounting grew under Henry I
Britain's Prime Minister has formally been First Lord of the Treasury since Robert Walpole in 1721

current_meaning: the funds of a state or institution; the department that manages them
